Ammishaddai
am-mih-SHAD-eye
proper noun
Hebrew Ammishadday (H5996), the Almighty is my kinsman, or people of the Almighty — from am (H5971), people, kindred, and Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty.

Biblical Definition

Ammishaddai was of the tribe of Dan in the exodus generation, and Scripture names him five times, always as the father of Ahiezer, prince and captain of Dan (Num 1:12; 2:25; 7:66, 71; 10:25). Dan's post in the order of march was the rereward — the rear guard of all the camps, the place that gathers up the stragglers and takes the first blow from behind. Ahiezer, whose name means my brother is help, commanded there; his father's name means the Almighty is my kinsman. Read together, the household confession is one of covenant kinship under God: the Almighty is not a distant power but a near relation, and therefore the rear of the column is as safe as the front. Am is the word of belonging — the word in I will take you to me for a people, and I will be to you a God (Exo 6:7) — and to join it to Shaddai is to claim the Almighty as one's own kindred. That is not presumption; it is the covenant. Ruth's thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God (Rut 1:16) makes the same claim from the outside, and the LORD honoured it.

Origin & Era

A Danite of the exodus generation, father of Ahiezer prince of Dan; his name means the Almighty is my kinsman.

AMMISHADDAI, Hebrew Ammishadday, the Almighty is my kinsman, or people of the Almighty.

A man of the tribe of Dan in the generation that came out of Egypt.

Father of Ahiezer, prince and captain of the children of Dan.

Named five times in the book of Numbers, always as the father of Ahiezer.

Dan marched as the rereward of all the camps throughout their hosts.

Key Scripture

Num 1:12 — "Of Dan; Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai."

Num 2:25 — "The standard of the camp of Dan shall be on the north side by their armies: and the captain of the children of Dan shall be Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai."

Num 7:66 — "On the tenth day Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, prince of the children of Dan, offered:"

Num 10:25 — "And the standard of the camp of the children of Dan set forward, which was the rereward of all the camps throughout their hosts: and over his host was Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai."

Modern Corruption

Nearness to God is offered as a feeling to be cultivated; the covenant makes it a legal kinship God Himself establishes.

expand to see more

Much modern devotional teaching treats intimacy with God as an atmosphere the believer produces — by music, by solitude, by the right posture of heart — and measures nearness by how near it feels. The covenant works the other way. Kinship with God is a status conferred by God and sealed by blood, and it holds when the feeling is absent. I will be to you a God, and ye shall be to me a people is a declaration, not a description of Israel's mood. Ammishaddai's name asserts a relation, and a relation either exists or it does not.

The New Testament raises the claim higher than kinsman to son. Ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father (Rom 8:15), and adoption is a legal act, irrevocable, made by the Father's will and not by the child's performance. The principle to recover is that the believer's standing does not fluctuate with his sense of it. A man marching in the rereward, at the dusty back of the column with the enemy behind him, is as truly kin to the Almighty as the man carrying the standard at the front.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Ammishadday (H5996), from am (H5971), people, kindred, and Shaddai (H7706), the Almighty.

expand to see more

Hebrew am (H5971) — people, kindred, nation; the covenant word of belonging, ye shall be to me a people (Exo 6:7).

Hebrew Shaddai (H7706) — the Almighty; the patriarchal name of God (Exo 6:3).

Hebrew Ammishadday (H5996) — the Danite father of Ahiezer, Numbers 1:12, 2:25, 7:66, 7:71, 10:25.

Hebrew goel (H1350) — kinsman-redeemer, the near relation with the right to buy back; the office Boaz filled for Ruth.

Greek huiothesia (G5206) — adoption as sons; whereby we cry, Abba, Father (Rom 8:15).
